transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Dave Mattingly.
Saudi Arabia and Yemen have exchanged more deadly attacks in the last 24 hours.
NPR's Ayyub Etrari reports from Dubai.
Saudi Arabia's aviation authority says the airport and the eastern city of Dammam was
attacked causing fatalities and injuries.
It also says the attack caused damage to the airport, but gave no further details.
Yemen's Houthis have been attacking Saudi airports for several weeks.
Commercial flights to the capital, Riyadh, remain suspended following deadly attacks
there 12 days ago.
The State Department says it's ordered the departure of some U.S. government employees
and their families from Saudi Arabia due to these attacks.
The Saudi Energy Ministry says another attack on an oil field in the east killed two laborers.
Meanwhile, the Houthis say Saudi-led airstrikes killed at least 20 people.
Among them, women and children across Yemen, Ayyub Etrari, NPR News, Dubai.
President Trump heads to Iowa today to continue campaigning for Republican candidates ahead
of the November midterm elections.
They're now less than two weeks away.
NPR's Franco Ordonez says the president was in South Carolina last night attending a rally
for GOP Senator Darlene Graham, the sister of the late Senator Lindsey Graham.
President Trump urged the very enthusiastic crowd at Clemson University to show up at
the polls to help elect Darlene Graham and other Republicans.
Trump spoke of Graham carrying on the legacy of her brother, who was a close ally to the
president.
I asked Arlene to run, and after a little thought, because it's a very big decision,
it really is, it's a big decision because I'm loving it.
She said yes, and I was very happy about it.
Graham is in a surprisingly tight race for such a red state, running against Democrat
Annie Andrews.
But Trump has struggled politically as the war in Iran has dragged on, and gas prices
have surged.
Franco Ordonez, NPR News.
Democrats and some Republicans are denouncing a GOP campaign ad critical of Ohio Democratic
gubernatorial candidate Amy Acton.
It features Acton's estranged mother and spotlights the abuse she experienced as a child.
At a campaign stop in Columbus on behalf of Republican gubernatorial candidate Vivek Ramaswamy,
Vice President Vance defended the ad.
He told reporters he was disgusted by fellow Republicans who've been critical of it.
Acton was asked by CNN about the ad and Ramaswamy.
You know, I'd hoped he wouldn't sink this low, but of course he did.
In the ad, Acton's birth mother, Donna Arthur, calls her daughter a liar and suggests she
has mental health issues.
Arthur lost custody of her children after their stepfather was indicted for raping Acton as
a child.
While street futures are lower this morning, Dow futures are off more than 300 points.
This is NPR News from Washington.
Shattered windows from large hail and downed trees from strong winds are reported in areas
of northern and central Arizona.
That's after storms moved through the region.
Mesa and Flagstaff are among the areas affected.
A meteorologist with the National Weather Service calls the storms unusual for this
time of year.
Some of the hail was the size of golf balls.
Flood watches and warnings remain in effect in much of Arizona this morning.
A new survey shows the monthly cost for health plans through employers in the U.S. rose this
year.
NPR's Selena Simmons-Duffin says the increase was about the same as inflation.
The nonpartisan health research organization KFF just released its annual survey of nearly
2,000 employers about their health benefits.
Health insurance costs have been going up fast for years, so even though this year's
increase is 5 percent, about the same as wage growth and inflation, all those increases
add up.
On average, premiums for a family of four now cost $28,000 per year, says Matthew Ray
of KFF.
Which is just a ton of money.
It's basically the cost of a new car every year just to keep a family of four insured.
Of that total, the survey found the share that workers pay rose to more than $7,400
per year on average.
So even people with great health coverage through work are putting a lot of their income towards
health insurance.
Selena Simmons-Duffin, NPR News.
Tesla is reporting a sharp drop in third quarter earnings.
That income was down 44 percent from the same period a year ago.
I'm Dave Mattingly in Washington.
Want to hear this podcast without sponsor breaks?
Amazon Prime members can listen to NPR News now, sponsor free through Amazon Music.
Or you can also support NPR's vital journalism and get NPR+ at plus.npr.org.
Plus dot NPR dot org.

topics.text: Saudi Arabia and Yemen exchange deadly attacks, including strikes on Dammam airport and an eastern oil field
President Trump rallies in South Carolina for Senate candidate Lindsey Graham's sister Darlene Graham ahead of midterms
Republican ad featuring Amy Acton's estranged mother draws Democratic and GOP criticism; Vance defends it
Severe storms in Arizona shatter windows and down trees, with golf-ball-sized hail in Mesa and Flagstaff
KFF survey finds employer health plan premiums rose about 5 percent this year, to roughly $28,000 for a family
Tesla third quarter earnings fall 44 percent from a year earlier
